rule: Background 7; column 0 is a 6 stripe and column 1 is background; bars lie on even rows starting at x=2 or 3. A row y is released iff the first non-background cells of rows y-1 and y+1 have the same colour, sit at the same x, and row y is background at that x. For each released row, (y,0) becomes 7. A walker starts at (y,1) heading right, moves while the next cell is background, and when blocked turns into the unique perpendicular background neighbour whose two flanks are equal and non-background. With 0 or 2 openings it stops, and a 6 is written there. All walks read the input.
scope: Constructive coloured-bar corridors with a left marker stripe, exact release predicates, forks and blocked turns, right/up/down/left legs and forceable three-turn routes; width10..30, odd height11..29, one through seven released markers subject to bar capacity. Explicit rectangles replay all canonical scenes.

authored_scope: Random mode: width 10..30 (default samples the full range, including 30), odd height 11..29, 1..5 corridors (at most (height+1)//4). Route designs: open, cap, badturn, fork, down/up, downstop/upstop, downturn/upturn, plus zigdown/zigup. The zig routes go right, then into a vertical channel, then turn LEFT along a gap row, then hit a blocker and make a third turn back through 1-3 split bars, ending on a bar with symmetric flanks or at the grid edge. A 2-turn variant ends on the left leg. zigzag=True forces at least one 3-turn zig route, zigzag=False forbids zig routes, and None forces one in about 35% of scenes. Hard negatives: blocked pairs (condition 3), same-colour adjacent singles with different starts (condition 2), isolated stub decoys (only condition 2 fails: equal-colour stubs at different x, with the bar row background at the upper stub), same-x in-bar decoys (only condition 3 fails), and in-bar different-x decoys. Not supported: random walks with more than 3 turns or a second leftward leg, bars starting at columns other than 2 or 3, a broken stripe or non-background column 1, even heights in random mode, and palette control. Fixtures are replayed from explicit segments, with dead ends derived by the local walker.
authored_constraints: Colour 7 is strictly the most frequent input colour; this is checked for every random scene because the reference uses the mode as background.
Column 0 is all 6 and column 1 is all 7 in every input row; segment colours are never 6 or 7.
The set of released rows equals the set of designed corridor rows exactly; this is checked with a local copy of the release test.
Every corridor's planned dead end equals the local walker's end. This is a bounded consistency filter; the endpoints come from the latent route.
Corridor pairs share colour and start; adjacent non-paired bars never share both colour and start.
Channel columns stay background along their path; cells inside channels or bar ranges cause rejection; lo/hi extents of every bar must be consistent.
Split bars keep at least two cells on the left and one on the right of each gap, and their gaps are not adjacent.
Decoy stubs are the first non-background cell of their gap row; isolated decoys put the upper stub where the bar row is background.
Retries are bounded at 3000. After 400 failures, alternate attempts restrict non-forced corridors to local designs so dense or narrow requests stay feasible.
